questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. What happens if the air supply leaks out of an older trailer's air brake system?

options.text: The trailer will have no brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks out, the brakes will not work. The trailer wheels will spin freely with no stopping power.

questions.question: When braking a trailer with anti-lock brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Use extra braking force to make the brakes work.
Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.
questions.explanation: With anti-lock brakes, brake the same way you normally would. Do not pump the brakes or use extra force. Let the anti-lock system work on its own.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and connects to the ____ valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves. These valves allow trailer brakes to work quickly.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle is empty, its stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have:
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle has less weight. Less weight means lower traction. The stiff springs and strong brakes work better with a full load.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer during coupling, what should you do next?
questions.explanation: After connecting the air lines to the trailer during coupling, supply air to the trailer. This is an important step in properly coupling a trailer.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs are more likely to roll over. The heavy cargo raises the center of gravity, making rollover more likely than with an empty rig.

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles requires ____ operating single vehicles.

options.text: About the same level of skill as

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They require higher driving skills to operate safely.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer attached. Drivers must be careful when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: How should a driver test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully and turn off the engine. Then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to the emergency position when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, how should you keep it from moving?

options.text: Park it against a wall or other vehicle.
Park it on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling or moving.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer to your tractor, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Lock the trailer brakes before backing your tractor under the trailer to couple it. This is an important safety step.

questions.question: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels:

options.text: Follow the same path as the front wheels.
Follow a different path than the front wheels.
Are not a concern for the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow a different path than the front wheels.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels when turning a corner. This is called off-tracking. Longer vehicles have more off-tracking than shorter vehicles.

questions.question: On a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops to between:
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, you should:

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.
Back on a curve toward the driver's side.
Back on a curve toward the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back on a curve toward the driver's side.
questions.explanation: Back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: To check if a vehicle made before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look inside the back of the fifth wheel.
Look for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes to see if it has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in the ____ position.
questions.explanation: The air supply control should be in the "normal" position when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, you should:

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel.
Push the accelerator to the floor when starting from a stop.

questions.explanation: Steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering moves can cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: Put the trailer air supply control in "emergency" position to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start your trip. Pull out the trailer air supply control or put it in "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly and make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: If the trailer's spring brakes do not release when you press the tractor air supply control, you should:

options.text: Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.explanation: Check that the air line connections are properly attached and sealed. All equipment must work properly before you start your trip.
